N° 11Civic education and debate platform, Cameroon2026

Terre, Peuples & République

A map is not a land title. A platform that separates four things politicians mix up on purpose (a people's history, the development of land, the legal status of a plot and citizenship) and shows, from the Constitution, the 1974 land law and dated research, that every Cameroonian has the same rights everywhere.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Before the 2026 local elections, a slogan, Le Littoral aux Littoraliens, called for elected offices in the Littoral region to be reserved for people whose families originate there. The debate ran on rumour and anger: administrative regions were treated as ethnic property, land rights as a matter of ancestry, and the articles of law that do mention origin were either hidden or stretched. Few people could check what the law, the land registry and historians actually say.

02

What it does

A long-form text and two opinion pieces set out the position: no Cameroonian is a stranger in their own country, and arriving first, or meeting the colonizer first, gives no one more power. Every module then lets visitors check it. A timeline separates oral tradition, documented fact and law. A map compares the seven provinces of 1972 with the ten regions since 1983. A land lab walks through nine plots, from a titled house to a forest reserve, and asks each time whether the owner's origin changes anything. A simulation turns bush into a town, then a decree draws a new region and no plot changes hands. A test shows that the law never defines who is autochtone. A fact checker corrects claims from both sides, a contradiction page gives the opposing side its strongest arguments and lets visitors vote, Libre Arbitre, a debate agent with a carved owl emblem, answers extreme statements with facts, law and a question, and a public debate collects positions and replies.

03

How it is built

React with Preact for a light bundle on mobile networks, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind, hosted on Vercel. The debate and the votes run on Supabase Postgres with row-level security: visitors can read and post but never edit or delete, a trigger limits flooding, and reports hide a message automatically. Libre Arbitre answers from a verified knowledge base in the browser; an optional AI mode runs in a Supabase Edge Function with rate limits and stays off until a key is added. Facts are tied to 39 dated sources, from the Constitution and the 1974 and 1976 land texts to Eckert, Barbier, Mainet and Schler, and the site states plainly what it could not verify.
